📚 Today you learned

Marketable vs. Resting Limit Orders

A buy limit is "marketable" the instant the market price sits at or below your limit — it should fill almost immediately, same as a market order but with a price ceiling. It's "resting" when the market is still above your limit — it just sits on the book waiting. Your two live GTC orders illustrate both states perfectly right now. GOOG's buy limit is $365; GOOG last traded around $353 — that limit is marketable and should have already filled (worth confirming in IBKR, since portfolio.json still shows zero shares). AXTI's buy limit is $58; AXTI is trading near $88.58 after an earnings-driven run — that limit is deeply resting, miles from marketable, and won't fill unless the stock gives back over a third of its move. Same order type, completely different real-world status, and the only way to tell them apart is checking current price against your limit — the order ticket alone won't tell you.

Also today: Order aging — a GTC order doesn't re-evaluate the thesis it was placed for; the longer it rests unfilled, the more likely the setup that justified the price has changed underneath it.
